Message from php85-8.5.12_2:

--
SECURITY: session upload progress (CVE-2026-115560, informational)

Until the next regular PHP bugfix release, session.upload_progress.enabled
should be 0. The shipped php.ini-production and php.ini-development now
set it, but existing php.ini files are never modified on upgrade, and
with no php.ini the compiled-in default (enabled) applies. If you
already applied this setting for CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp),
keep it; nothing further is needed.

The issue needs an unusual combination: session.serialize_handler set
to php_binary or php_serialize in configuration, switched to php at
runtime with ini_set() before session_start(), with upload progress
still enabled. Applications that never change the handler at runtime
can keep the feature enabled.

Check the effective value per SAPI (CLI and FPM/mod_php may load
different ini files):

    php -r 'var_dump(ini_get("session.upload_progress.enabled"));'

For FPM/mod_php, use phpinfo() from a web request. Ini files are read
from /usr/local/etc/php.ini and /usr/local/etc/php/*.ini.

Check both halves of the precondition:

    php -r 'var_dump(ini_get("session.serialize_handler"));'
    grep -rn serialize_handler /usr/local/www /usr/local/etc/php* \
        /usr/local/etc/apache2*

A match on one half alone is not vulnerable; the combination is. To
make runtime switching impossible in FPM, set in the pool config:

    php_admin_value[session.serialize_handler] = php

This breaks applications that legitimately need php_serialize at runtime.

After changing any setting, restart the PHP service, e.g.:

    service php_fpm restart

This notice will be removed once the fixed release is in the tree.
